newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas pares gains late, still up on weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas pares gains late, still up on weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures pared gains but remained higher late Monday in moderate trade, with heat in the Midwest and Northeast boosting physical prices and underpinning the complex.
At 1420 EDT, July was still up 2.5 cents at $2.26 per million British thermal units, while August was up the same at $2.26. Other deferreds remained 0.8 to 1.8 cents higher.

"There's definitely some good news out there for the bulls, but we seem to be stalling here. If we can close above $2.28 (basis July) today, I'd be more excited," a Texas trader said, referring to forecasts for more heat and some nuke outages.
PECO's 1,055 MW Limerick 1 nuclear power unit and GPU's 786 MW Three Mile Island 1 unit both were shut over the weekend for unscheduled repairs and were likely to remain down through the week.

These latest outages, added to long-term outages at two units at the Salem, N.J., facility, and three units at the Millstone plant in Connecticut, could leave the area tight on generation this week and help prop up gas prices ahead of bidweek later in the week, traders said.
Spot electricity prices in the Mid-Atlantic almost doubled Monday on news of the plant shutdowns amid the heat wave.

Chart traders said July's break today of double top resistance at $2.245 helped trigger some short covering but most agreed a close above the down trendline in the $2.28 area was needed to see higher numbers. Next resistance was seen in the $2.36-2.37 area and then at the contract high of $2.44. Support was pegged at the $2.151 double bottom, then at $2.13, $2.055 and $2.

In the cash, Louisiana Gulf Coast gas firmed almost a nickel Monday to the mid-to-high $2.20s. Midcon pipes gained a similar amount to about the $2.10 area. New York city gate gas was quoted almost a dime higher in the high-$2.50s.
NYMEX said 23,612 contracts traded at 1350 EDT.
NYMEX July natgas futures expire Thursday, June 26.
On KCBT, July was still up by two cents at $2.12, while deferreds were 2.5 to 4.5 cents higher. The East/West spread widened by one-half cent to 14.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
KCBT July natgas futures expire Wednesday, June 25.
